evidence.paraphrase: The page presents a single measure intended to summarize the common state of global supply-chain pressure across multiple transportation and survey indicators.
Ocean and air freight costs are combined with country-level purchasing-manager measures related to delivery times, backlogs, and purchased stocks.
Standardized indicators are combined through a factor framework, with demand-related influences accounted for so the resulting index is interpreted as supply pressure.
The index is expressed in historical standard deviations, depends on coverage and loading stability, and does not by itself quantify causal pass-through into U.S. consumer prices.

executive_summary: The New York Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index compresses transportation-cost and manufacturing-survey indicators into a standardized latent measure of global supply pressure. The construction is valuable as a cost-push factor only if shipping and PMI inputs, demand adjustment, missing observations, normalization, loadings, and pandemic-regime sensitivity remain visible; the index is not itself an identified estimate of U.S. inflation pass-through.

method_routes.aggregation_role: external-supply state factor; any U.S. inflation pass-through requires a separate identified or predictive node
method_routes.estimand: common standardized supply-chain pressure in the observed shipping and PMI panel
method_routes.formula: standardize X_t; remove registered demand component; estimate common factor GSCPI_t=lambda'X_t+e_t
method_routes.identification_strategy: latent-factor extraction after registered demand adjustment; not causal inflation identification
identifying_assumptions: standardized inputs share a stable common supply component
input direction and normalization are fixed by recipe
missing indicators and changing country coverage are handled without future information
method_routes.sample_definition: monthly global shipping and PMI indicators available at each index vintage

questions.horizon_text: current global supply state and near-term cost pressure
questions.question_text: What common global supply-chain pressure is contained in transportation-cost and manufacturing-survey indicators, separate from broad demand conditions?
